pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour of the music school in this workspace. Share it with the director, every teacher and the front office.
: each student's instrument, level, teacher, parent, practice goal, make-up lessons owed, tuition owed and billed to date.
: the weekly schedule with room, teacher and the practice set for the week.
: monthly charges, due, overdue and paid.
: every performance with the piece, the date and whether an accompanist is needed.
: every instrument, who has it, the deposit, the condition and when it is due back.
Monday: lessons and make-ups for the week confirmed.
Every day: teachers mark lessons and set practice.
Thursday: overdue tuition followed up; rentals due back called.
Friday: the director reads the Dashboard: awaiting payment, performances in the next two weeks, rentals out.
Every morning: today's lessons and rooms
Every week: overdue tuition, make-ups owed
Every month: tuition billed on the first, rentals reviewed
Every term: recitals planned, levels reviewed, rental sizes checked

The director owns enrollment, the teacher schedule, recitals and policies. Teachers own lessons, practice plans, levels and performance choices. The front office owns tuition, rentals and make-up booking.

Every new student starts with a trial lesson. The teacher writes the level and a practice goal after it, and the office follows up within two days with a lesson time, the tuition plan and, if needed, a rental instrument in the right size.
Students appear by first name and last initial. Parents' phone numbers and payment details are confidential and stay with the office.
Rename instruments, rooms and levels to match your school and delete the sample rows once your own are in. Edit any cell in place and drag cards between columns; totals update on their own.
The school at a glance. Charts read the live tables.

text.text: A recital is the moment families see what a term of lessons bought. Make it short, warm and well organized, and every child should leave proud.
Book the hall and pick the date with the director. Avoid school holidays and exam weeks.

Book an accompanist for every student who needs one.
Pieces are learned; now the work is polishing and memory.
Set the order: youngest and newest first, a mix of instruments, the strongest players at the end of each half.
Keep it under 75 minutes. Two short recitals beat one long one.
One rehearsal with the accompanist for each student who needs one
Program printed with names (first name and last initial) and pieces
Families told the time, the place and when to arrive

A teacher backstage keeps the order and sends each student on.
